Subject: Timing for PO issuance and billing inputs for Q2 bookings

Hi Priyom / Laura,

We're finalizing our internal procurement timeline for the services that will convert to bookings in Q2. Finance wants a short checklist of what ACME needs to issue a PO that will allow us to invoice and recognize revenue in April. Specific asks are:

- Exact PO fields we require (billing account, remit-to, special codes)
- Whether we need an executed SOW before PO acceptance
- Any additional compliance docs (tax forms, vendor setup lead time)
- Target date to receive the PO to hit April recognition

Can you send a one-page readiness note plus any templates we can attach to the internal PO request?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Timing for PO issuance and billing inputs for Q2 bookings

Mike — thanks for the note. See a concise summary below and two attachments (billing-readiness-checklist.xlsx, acme_po_template.pdf) to hand to your procurement team.

High-level gating items to enable invoice issuance and bookings recognition in April:

1) Signed commercial document: We need either an executed SOW or a signed Order Form that cites the Master Services Agreement. If you expect the PO to arrive before signatures, we can hold a PO number for provisioning but cannot invoice/recognize until paperwork is complete.

2) Purchase Order: PO must include: purchaser legal name, remit-to address, billing contact (name + email), PO number, line items (product codes we provide in the template), and total contract value. If procurement needs internal GL or cost-center codes we can include an additional mapping column in the template.

3) Billing setup requirements: Standard vendor setup (W-9 for US entities) — no SOC or KYC exchange required for standard cloud SaaS. If ACME requires special invoicing cadence (net-30 vs net-45) or split invoices by delivery milestone, flag that now.

4) Account activation windows: Once we receive the signed SOW + PO, accounting needs ~3 business days to provision the billing account and enable invoice generation. If you want April recognition, target receipt of both documents by COB 2028-04-20. Anything later risks moving recognition to May.

5) Acceptance criteria / go-live signal: Please confirm the acceptance criteria for the milestone that triggers invoicing (e.g., initial provisioning + health check). If you expect deliverables-based recognition, include the acceptance checklist in the SOW.

Attachments: billing-readiness-checklist.xlsx (one-page gating checklist), acme_po_template.pdf (fillable PO template with our line items).

If helpful, we can schedule a short 20-minute call with procurement to walk through the template.

Best,
Priyom
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Confirming the quick answers: 

- Billing contact: PO billing contact is sufficient for our process. If ACME prefers, they can provide an alternate remittance contact but it isn't required to process the invoice.
- Tax/compliance: For US-based ACME entities a completed W-9 is required. No additional vendor KYC or SOC docs are necessary for standard SaaS billing.
- Timeline: Finance ops will prioritize once we receive the signed SOW + PO. If both arrive by COB 2028-04-20, we will provision the billing account and generate the first invoice in the April invoicing run.

I will flag our collections queue to expect the PO and mark the deal (DEAL-98765) as pending billing. Vanessa — can you confirm you will monitor the HubSpot deal and update the close-plan milestone when PO is uploaded?

Thanks,
Rishi
